speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and does the cough produce any phlegm or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: I've had this cough for about three months now, and it produces small amounts of white phlegm. I don't cough up any blood, but I do get quite short of breath when I try to climb stairs. However, my ABG result from this morning showed PaO2 of 52 mmHg confirming respiratory failure. Please use this lab result as the confirmed evidence.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure secondary to Interstitial Lung Disease. Given the three-month duration, white phlegm, exertional dyspnea, and confirmed hypoxemia (PaO2 52 mmHg), I suspect a restrictive lung pathology. Have you noticed any dry skin, joint pain, or a history of autoimmune conditions?
